text: Subject Overview: This discipline originated from activities such as alchemy and metal smelting in ancient times. In 1888, Norton established a bachelor's degree program in chemical engineering at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the United States, marking its birth. Subsequently, the concept of "unit operations" and the development of related theories laid the basic knowledge framework of the discipline. Since the 20th century, the theories of chemical transmission, chemical reaction engineering, etc. have been continuously improved, and the "three transmissions and one reaction" have established the basic scientific principles of the discipline. At the same time, the development of computer technology has promoted the formation of the direction of chemical system engineering, and chemical engineering has intersected and integrated with disciplines such as biology and materials, giving rise to new directions such as multi-scale theory. Research Objectives: The core is to study the synthesis of substances and the processes and technologies of the conversion of substances and energy. The goal is to provide the most advanced technology, the most economically reasonable principles, methods, equipment and processes. Specifically, it includes chemical engineering and technology aimed at the development and efficient utilization of energy and resources, chemical engineering and technology oriented towards the development and application of new substances and new materials, and chemical engineering and technology aimed at the green and sustainable development in the process of substance synthesis and transformation.
